html:
Toba-Lengua is an old name for a people of the Paraguayan Chaco now usually called Enenlhet, or Toba-Maskoy. They live west of the Paraguay River in the department of Presidente Hayes. They speak a language of the Enlhet-Enenlhet family, related to Enxet and Enlhet, and are not related to the Toba (Qom) of Argentina despite the name.

They lived by hunting, fishing and gathering in the wet and dry Chaco. From the late 1800s Paraguay sold the Chaco to foreign companies, and many worked on cattle ranches and at the tannin factories along the river. The Chaco War and the arrival of settlers took more of their land. Their relatives include the Enenlhet.
